parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a parent federal document/entry regime (sex-binary passport rules, X-marker ban, visa refusal and fraud findings for document discrepancy — travelers stranded abroad, foreign advisories issued) with a division that mandates birth-sex restroom use across state buildings, schools and prisons, backed by identification checks, an escalated enforcement inquiry, and a first arrest with 24 hours' detention in a men's ward. Marker changes are constitutionally barred statewide; no gender-identity discrimination or hate-crime coverage exists; courts upheld custody denial of surgery. A 'Do Not Travel' tier and sustained hostile legislation confirm trajectory. No identity offence or execution risk exists, and enforcement episodes are few, but the tier-1 universal facility exposure plus federal document exposure carry no working remedy.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal order ends self-selected markers and X-passports; visa officers instructed to refuse where documents cast doubt on sex, with possible lifetime fraud ineligibility; passport confiscation stranding travelers reported.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid until expiration; litigation pending; fraud finding not automatic and has limited waivers.
entry_documents.interaction: Division's definition act barring marker changes compounds federal record-matching; document discrepancy can escalate to refusal or fraud finding before entry.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Trans woman held 24 hours in men's ward after restroom arrest; federal prisons adopted conversion-therapy-style policies (hair, hormone removal); immigration custody reports of beatings, solitary, sexual abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Facility restroom law does not govern cell assignment; courts denied immunity but affirmed surgery refusal as permissible medical choice.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Division restroom law reaches prisons as to restroom use only; federal custody practices apply to federal detainees regardless of division protections.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Universal birth-sex restroom rule in state buildings, schools, universities from 4 Dec 2025 with $25k/$125k fines; federal buildings barred to identity-congruent use by executive order; trespass offence possible in 4 states.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Trespass requires willful entry plus refusal to depart, with exemptions; 29 states plus capital have no mapped ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor in state or federal buildings faces overlapping rules; the arrest precedent shows the rule reaches individuals, not just facility operators.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care banned for minors since 2023; DOJ subpoenaed under-19 patient records; LGBTQ youth lifeline services shut down; federal proposals barring insurance reimbursement for under-18 trans care.
care_services.protection: Adult care not banned; injunctions have blocked several parental-investigation directives.
care_services.interaction: An adult travelling with a trans minor cannot obtain youth care here and risks record scrutiny; resident-facing mainly, but constrains travelling families.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Official definitions enact binary sex; counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups; law-enforcement tip-line drives enforcement; officials justify checks as privacy protection.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Reward criteria do not list gender ideology; strategy states counterterrorism powers won't target mere disagreement; statements remain contested in court.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State framing plus federal 'gender ideology' posture legitimizes uneven, invasive enforcement warned of by opponents.

minors_guardians.exposure: Parental-rights statute mandates misgendering in schools; EO directs criminal investigation of schools facilitating social transition; child-abuse directives previously ordered investigations of affirming parents (partly enjoined).
minors_guardians.protection: Injunctions blocked some directives; five DAs refused compliance.
minors_guardians.interaction: A visiting family with a trans minor faces care denial and a school system under active federal investigation; minors amplify document-mismatch exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 44 recorded trans-women killings 2008–2025 (about 7.6/100k trans women/yr), the national worst in absolute terms; hate-crime statute excludes gender identity; city repealed LGBTQ ordinance; Pride events suspended.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime statute and 2020 employment ruling apply; several cities bar identity discrimination.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: No state bias-motivated-violence coverage means identity-based attacks get no penalty enhancement; general homicide baseline not available for comparison.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: July 2026 assessment places state in top 'Do Not Travel' tier; no effective state complaint route; enforcement guidance unclear with no documented outcome to challenges.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Federal passport suit and EO challenges pending; legal-aid FAQ exists; some orders enjoined.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Pending litigation means exposure fluctuates by travel date, but no remedy has yet altered the operative facility or document rules.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like Veluna, this state imposes a universal birth-sex facility rule reaching visitors with no exemption obtainable, courts have upheld comparable rules, and complaints secure no relief. It sits slightly above 0.35-A because the trespass offence requires refusal to depart, enforcement episodes are few, and no identity offence exists — but slightly below it in remedy terms given active DOJ enforcement and a documented arrest with men's-ward detention.

Very close analogue: publicly funded birth-sex bathroom rule upheld, no presentation offence, ordinary politeness in private settings. This jurisdiction rates below 0.45-A because it adds documented individual arrest and custody in a men's ward, a 'Do Not Travel' assessment, a federal document/visa regime, and custody care denial affirmed on appeal — 0.45-A had none of these.

Isvera lacks any universal facility ban and has functioning bias prosecution and refunds. This jurisdiction sits clearly below it: the tier-1 facility rule with identification checks is inescapable for the outed visitor, gender identity is excluded from state hate-crime coverage, and no working remedy exists — recurring service friction plus partial remedies cannot compare to enforced exclusion.

Avalet accepts foreign markers, audits facilities, and convictions follow assaults. This case is materially lower: marker changes are banned, federal documents are forced to birth sex, visas may be refused on sex discrepancy, and facilities exclude by birth sex with fines and a documented arrest — an unremedied tier-1 exposure 0.65-A does not have.

parsed.synthesis: Three layers interact into one operative system. At entry, the federal document regime can refuse or delay a traveller whose papers cast doubt on sex, with a possible lifetime fraud finding — raising discovery probability before arrival. Inside the state, the birth-sex restroom statute reaches every state building, school and university; identification checks and one arrest with 24 hours in a men's ward show it operates on individuals, while fines drive facility compliance and DOJ escalation signals continued enforcement. Recourse is thin: no state discrimination law, hate-crime coverage excludes gender identity, courts affirmed custody care denial, and litigation remains unresolved. Social friction (repealed ordinances, suspended Pride) reinforces official hostility without adding an identity offence. For an adult with a minor, the youth care ban and record subpoenas add a further constraint. Absence of a criminal identity offence and few documented enforcement episodes keep this out of the high-risk tiers, but the unremedied universal facility exposure plus federal document exposure anchors it in elevated risk.
